newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Meridor backs capital market reform.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Meridor backs capital market reform.

text.p: Israeli Finance Minister Dan Meridor said a committee's recommendations on capital market reform were "acceptable" to him and he would submit the proposal to the government on October 13.

"The recommendations have proper incentives for encouraging long-term savings and important social aspects because they try to guarantee long-term savings for pension," the minister said in a statement.
Meridor said the report provides solutions to the problem of creating long-term funds for the mortgage market.
He expressed disappointment in those who hurried to criticise the report before they had read it entirely.
"These hasty reactions could harm an issue that is very important to the Israeli economy," the statement said.
Meridor noted the critics did not propose alternative solutions to the problems in the capital markets. "Therefore, they must think the status quo is the preferable situation," he said.
Treasury sources said that while Meridor adopts most of the recommendations he has reservations concerning a few minor points.
A government-appointed committee led by Finance Ministry Director General David Brodett on Tuesday presented Meridor with a sweeping proposal for reform in Israel's capital markets.
The report provoked widespread outcry as it calls for taxing short-term savings and would lower the amount pension funds can invest in special high-yielding governnment bonds.
